jp: このパン{は|wa-topic}おいしそうです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: This bread looks tasty, doesn't it?
why: ね invites the listener to share your reaction to something you are both looking at.

jp: このスーパー{は|wa-topic}野菜[やさい]{が|ga-subject}安[やす]いです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: Vegetables are cheap at this supermarket, aren't they?
why: ね seeks the listener's agreement about something you both can see.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}レジ{が|ga-subject}すいています{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: The checkout is empty today, isn't it?
why: ね asks the listener to agree with an observation you both share.

jp: あの時計[とけい]{は|wa-topic}高[たか]そうです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: That watch looks expensive, doesn't it?
why: ね seeks agreement with a shared impression of something in view.

jp: お金[かね]{が|ga-existence}ない時[とき]{は|wa-topic}、困[こま]ります{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: It's hard when you have no money, isn't it?
why: ね invites the listener to agree with a feeling both of you know well.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]{の|no-possessive}食事[しょくじ]{は|wa-topic}お金[かね]{が|ga-subject}かかります{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: Daily meals cost money, don't they?
why: ね asks the listener to agree with something you both experience.

jp: セール{の|no-possessive}日[ひ]{は|wa-topic}人[ひと]{が|ga-subject}たくさん来[き]ます{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: Lots of people come on sale days, don't they?
why: ね seeks agreement about something familiar to both speaker and listener.
